scope: offline only; no flash, no COM, no RF, no probe, no cryptography, no keys, no network
what_this_closes: the admission and scheduler counters existed since phases 1.2 and 1.3 but were not observable from the host, so nothing issue #5 asks to be measured -- classification outcomes, ACK suppression, per-context TX accounting, fairness -- could actually be read off a running device. STATS is the only place they become visible

verb.scope: global and read-only. ctx is refused with ctx_not_scoped, as on INFO and END
verb.field_set: id and boot. Not session-scoped, because the report covers both contexts and is not an action on either
verb.enum_placement: M_STATS is appended to management_kind_t rather than inserted, because the verbs[] table is indexed by that enum and an insertion would silently renumber every verb after it. The loop bound is now MANAGEMENT_VERB_COUNT rather than a literal 13, which is what made the old table safe to extend by hand and is no longer trusted to be

two_defects_in_my_own_earlier_code_fixed.why_it_mattered: every other reply record carries the host id it was asked with, and host/probe.py awaits a reply by matching kind and id. A STATS record without one could never be awaited: the bounded wait would simply time out, and the formatter's 98 passing checks would not have noticed because nothing awaited it
two_defects_in_my_own_earlier_code_fixed.fix: the formatter takes host_id and emits id=, and its test now asserts the field is present rather than only that the line formatted

two_defects_in_my_own_earlier_code_fixed.what: sched_backstop_fired was dead state: set when the scheduler's deadline backstop fired, never read
two_defects_in_my_own_earlier_code_fixed.why_it_mattered: the condition it recorded is a real fault -- the lifecycle lost a frame it owned -- and writing it to a flag nobody reads means the fault is invisible except as a stop with no stated cause
two_defects_in_my_own_earlier_code_fixed.fix: removed, and both conditions now count into sched_routing_faults: a completion the scheduler refused to route, and the backstop firing. They are one failure class -- the lifecycle and the scheduler disagreeing about which frame owns the radio -- and deserve one observable counter. Both still stop the runtime, and both counters saturate rather than wrap

firmware_counters_added_to_the_record.starved_polls: a context that was due to poll and could not be offered, because its own queue was still occupied. This is the fairness number issue #5 asks to be bounded, and it lives in main.c rather than in either stats struct

answered_before_the_capture_loss_check: deliberate. Every other verb is refused once out_drop or a gate drop is seen, because acting on lost evidence is unsafe. A read-only report is the opposite case: when evidence has been lost the counters are the most useful thing left to read, and refusing to show them is the opposite of what a diagnostic is for
host_side: probe.py names STATS in the reply-kind map and in GLOBAL_VERBS. Without the first it would have hung on its own request; without the second it would have sent a ctx the firmware refuses

test_dual_records.note: 98 before; the three new checks assert id=, starved_polls= and the trailing routing_faults=

native.two_hosts: identical results in the cloud container and in the device VM

live_record_through_the_real_dispatcher.method: firmware_cli.exe, which compiles the actual src/main.c with a fake radio
live_record_through_the_real_dispatcher.sequence: INFO, BIND ctx=1, one MANAGEMENT_POLL on ctx1, then STATS
live_record_through_the_real_dispatcher.observed: ctx1_tx_accepted=1 ctx1_tx_terminal=1 ctx0_tx_accepted=0 ctx0_tx_terminal=0 ctx0_tx_queue=0 ctx1_tx_queue=0 starved_polls=0 routing_faults=0 routing_error=0 scheduler_starvation=0
live_record_through_the_real_dispatcher.reading: the one poll was accounted to the context that sent it and to no other, both queues drained, and the lifecycle and scheduler agreed throughout
live_record_through_the_real_dispatcher.scope_rules: STATS with ctx=1 refused as ctx_not_scoped; STATS without boot refused as field_set

arm_image.reproducible: two consecutive runs produced the same HEX hash
arm_image.reading: bss is unchanged, which is the expected shape: this phase adds the formatter (previously compiled in but unreferenced, so --gc-sections dropped it) and one parser verb, and the record is written through a stack buffer. A bss increase here would have meant the change had quietly added runtime state

still_not_done: the contract's generic TX verb is not implemented; nothing needs it until issue #6
no hardware gate has been prepared or reviewed, and no guard exists
the 32 bit microsecond clock wraps at about 71.6 minutes and main.c stops on a backwards clock, so a 60 minute soak must be designed around that rather than into it
